base_body_policy: adult female base body with adult anatomy-guided proportions; no Barbie/non-adult treatment
identity_goal: A realistic synthetic-person Gwen Stacy/Spider-Gwen inspired by Spider-Verse movie Gwen, not a flat movie/comic copy.
source_policy: Movie-frame Gwen references define identity, head shape, expression language, hair, eye color, and suit identity.
Realistic multi-view fan/concept turnarounds can help with 3D realism and body/suit views, but cannot be copied.
Comic strips are design references only: suit markings, color blocks, pose language, and recurring identity cues.
Do not use voice-actress photos, cosplayers, toys, or unrelated real people for likeness.
head_targets: asymmetrical blond/white side-swept hair with shaved/shorter side where reference shows it
recognizable Gwen brow shape and expressive eyebrow range
real eye sockets with blue-gray irises, movable eyes, eyelids, and catchlights
profile follows references: nose bridge, nose tip, lips, chin, jaw, ear, and neck depth
mouth opens naturally with teeth, tongue, lips, and speech shapes
subtle freckles/skin detail if approved from references
body_targets: not skin-tight painted anatomy; base body remains separate under wardrobe
suit silhouette should read as spandex/superhero suit when worn
hands and feet must remain correctly scaled and rigged
walk, turn, sit, look-around, and talk tests required
wardrobe_targets: Spider-Gwen suit is a wardrobe/morph garment layer, not the base body
hood, white upper layer, black torso/legs, pink web gloves/inner arms, teal shoes, and back markings should be separate named garment/material regions
support future normal clothes separately from the superhero suit
if the suit is treated as a normal garment, it needs stored, dressing, worn, removed, folded/hung states
if the suit is treated as a superhero morph/magic exception, record that separately and do not pretend it was physically dressed
